summary: The clearest structural signal in the data is the Exhaustion Short panel being blocked 6/6 times by the prev_day_rally gate — all missed stocks fell 5-8.7% from their highs on days with little or no prior rally, meaning the gate's core assumption (exhaustion only follows a prior rally) is empirically false and needs a redesign, not a nudge. The Trap Reversal panels (Bear and Bull) show 15 combined signals with 0 wins and 14 expirations, which is a systemic problem: the SL is anchored to the full day's extreme rather than the trap structure itself, producing risk-reward that looks favourable on paper but expires before it moves. Momentum Breakout has the only real win rate (28.6% bull, 12.5% bear) but the high expired count across both directions suggests entries are being taken too far from the breakout candle.

proposals.reasoning: Even if the OR-logic change above is not immediately implemented, the threshold of 6.0% is empirically too high: CROMPTON (actual_value 1.47%) and HINDUNILVR (1.38%) both fell 7-8.7% from highs, meaning meaningful exhaustion events occur after much smaller prior rallies. Lowering to 3.5% keeps the spirit of the gate (some prior upward pressure) while capturing mid-strength rallies. This is a secondary proposal to the logic_change above — if both are applied, the threshold reduction matters less, but in isolation it would have caught CROMPTON and HINDUNILVR at minimum.
proposals.expected_impact: Would pass 2-3 more of the 6 missed signals through this gate. Does not eliminate the need for the OR-logic change since BANDHANBNK's actual_value was -0.87% (a down day) and -6.21% — no threshold reduction alone fixes those.

proposals.title: Replace single-condition prev_day_rally gate with OR-logic: prior rally OR intraday gap-up OR high relative to 5-day range
proposals.proposed_change: The current gate requires BOTH prev_day_rally_pct >= EXH_PREV_DAY_RALLY_PCT (6.0%) AND cumul_rally_pct >= EXH_CUMUL_RALLY_PCT as a combined AND condition that fails if neither is met. Replace this with a three-way OR condition that passes if ANY of the following is true: (1) prev_day_rally_pct >= EXH_PREV_DAY_RALLY_PCT (unchanged, 6.0%), OR (2) cumul_rally_pct >= EXH_CUMUL_RALLY_PCT (unchanged, meaning a multi-day run qualifies even without a big single day), OR (3) a new gate: today's open gapped up >= EXH_GAP_UP_PCT above the prior close (suggested starting value: EXH_GAP_UP_PCT = 2.0, meaning a 2%+ gap-up open itself signals price was driven up into supply without requiring a prior-day rally). Insert this OR block in the same position as the existing prev_day_rally check, before the turnover threshold. The existing code already computes gap_pct later; compute it early from daily['Close'].iloc[-2] and today_bars['Open'].iloc[0] and use it here. HINDUNILVR (actual_value 1.38%, fell 8.72%) and DMART (actual_value 0.23%, fell 6.02%) both likely opened with a gap or were near multi-month highs — the 2% gap gate would capture those without lowering the bar for flat-open, no-rally stocks.
proposals.reasoning: The missed-signals data is unambiguous: 6 out of 6 missed exhaustion events were blocked solely by prev_day_rally. The actual_values for the blocking gate range from -6.21% to +1.47% — not even close to the 6.0% threshold. BANDHANBNK fell 7.32% on a day when the prior close was DOWN 0.87%; HINDUNILVR fell 8.72% on a day when the prior close was up only 1.38%. The premise that exhaustion only follows a prior-day rally is simply wrong — gap-up opens into prior supply also cause exhaustion selling. The fix is an OR-logic expansion, not a lower threshold, because lowering EXH_PREV_DAY_RALLY_PCT to near zero would destroy the gate's meaning entirely.
proposals.expected_impact: Would have caught approximately 3-4 of the 6 missed signals based on the sample (those with flat or modest prior-day moves but gap-up opens or high intraday positions). May slightly increase false-positive rate on low-rally, low-gap stocks — mitigated by the fact that the spike candle, volume, and turnover gates still apply downstream.

proposals.panel: Bear Trap Reversal / Bull Trap Reversal
proposals.title: Replace day-extreme SL with trap-structure SL: SL below the trap candle's low (bear trap) or above its high (bull trap)
proposals.proposed_change: Currently the SL for a Bear Trap (bullish) is set to round(day_low * 0.997, 2) — the full day's lowest low. For a Bull Trap (bearish) it's round(day_high * 1.003, 2). The day extreme is always worse (wider) than the trap candle itself because the day_low IS the trap's wicking low. Replace with a structure-based SL: for Bear Trap, SL = round(min(lows[trap_bar], lows[trap_bar-1 if trap_bar > 0 else trap_bar]) * 0.997, 2) — i.e., 0.3% below the trap bar's own low rather than the global day low (they are often identical, but this anchors the SL semantically to the trap candle). More importantly, add a new constant TRAP_MAX_SL_PCT = 1.5 and enforce: if risk / current_price * 100 > TRAP_MAX_SL_PCT, skip the signal (_dbg_fail 'sl_too_wide'). Insert this check immediately after the existing 'risk <= 0' guard. This prevents signals where the SL is so wide that T1 (1.5R) and T2 (3R) are never reached intraday.
proposals.reasoning: Bear Trap had 6 signals with 0 wins and 6 expirations; Bull Trap had 9 signals with 0 wins, 1 loss, and 8 expirations. A 94% expiration rate across 15 combined signals is not a signal-quality problem — it is a trade-plan problem. When the SL is the full day extreme (e.g., a stock that wicked to -2.5% intraday), T1 at 1.5R requires a +3.75% move from entry, which almost never happens intraday after a trap. By capping max SL at 1.5%, T1 becomes reachable at +2.25% from entry. Signals with SL > 1.5% should simply not be surfaced — they are structurally too wide for an intraday setup. The 0% win rate on a combined 15 signals with near-zero losses (only 1 total loss) confirms these are not wrong-direction calls; they simply never move enough to hit targets before 3:30 PM.
proposals.expected_impact: Will reduce total Trap signals generated (filtering out wide-SL setups), but the remaining signals will have achievable targets. Expected to convert expirations to wins on tight-structure traps. May drop signal count by 40-60% but win rate should improve from near-0% to a range comparable to Momentum Breakout.

proposals.panel: Momentum Breakout — Range Open + Clean PDH Break (Bullish) / Momentum Breakdown Bearish
proposals.title: Add maximum entry distance from breakout candle close: skip if current price is more than MB_MAX_CHASE_PCT above the breakout candle's close
proposals.proposed_change: Add a new constant MB_MAX_CHASE_PCT = 1.5. After the freshness check (n_bars - 1 - confirm > MB_FRESHNESS_BARS), add a gate: chase_pct = abs(current_price - closes[breakout_bar]) / closes[breakout_bar] * 100; if bullish and current_price > closes[breakout_bar] * (1 + MB_MAX_CHASE_PCT / 100): _dbg_fail(_debug, 'chasing_entry', symbol, chase_pct=round(chase_pct,2)); continue. Mirror for bearish. This prevents entries where price has already run 1.5%+ from the actual breakout candle close, which widens the true risk relative to the PDH-based SL that doesn't adjust for the chase.
proposals.reasoning: Momentum Breakout (bullish) has 7 total signals with 2 wins, 1 loss, and 4 expirations. The 4 expirations (57% of signals) suggest entries are frequently taken after price has already moved away from the structure. The freshness gate (MB_FRESHNESS_BARS = 6 bars = 30 min) allows entries up to 30 minutes after the confirm candle, during which time price may have already moved 1-2% above the breakout close, making T1 (1.5R above current price) unreachable. MB breakdown is even worse: 8 signals, 12.5% win rate, 5 expirations. Capping chase at 1.5% ensures the risk-reward is computed from a price still close to the structure, not from a chased entry.
proposals.expected_impact: Will reduce signal count (some signals will be filtered for chasing) but should improve win rate by ensuring T1/T2 remain geometrically achievable. The 2 wins in the bullish panel are likely from timely entries — the 4 expirations are likely from chased ones. Expected win rate improvement from ~28% to ~40-50% on a smaller sample.

proposals.title: Add daily ADR (Average Daily Range) filter to exclude low-volatility stocks that cannot reach T1 intraday
proposals.proposed_change: Add a new constant PDH_MIN_ADR_PCT = 1.8. Compute the Average Daily Range over the last 5 trading days: adr_pct = mean of [(high - low) / close * 100 for each of daily.iloc[-6:-1]]. If adr_pct < PDH_MIN_ADR_PCT, skip the signal (_dbg_fail 'adr_too_low'). Insert this check after the daily RSI check and before the volume check, since it's cheap to compute from already-loaded daily data. This filters stocks that structurally cannot move enough intraday for T1 (current_price + 1.5 * risk) to be reached before close.
proposals.reasoning: PDH Breakout has 0 wins, 3 losses, and 1 expiration across 4 signals — 0.0% win rate. While the sample is small (flag: 4 signals is too few for statistical certainty), the pattern of 3 losses (not expirations) suggests the breakouts are reversing rather than running. The RSI >= 60 and EMA200 filters should theoretically ensure trend alignment. A likely culprit is low-ATR stocks where PDH is only 0.5-0.8% above PDL — the SL (PDH * 0.997) is just 0.3% below PDH, but if the stock's daily range is only 1%, T1 requires a 0.45% move which is achievable, yet any small reversal triggers the SL. A minimum ADR of 1.8% ensures the stock has enough intrinsic volatility for the trade geometry to work. This is directional: 0/4 with 3 losses is suspicious and warrants a structural filter, not just a parameter nudge.
proposals.expected_impact: Will reduce PDH signals (filtering out low-ADR names). Given 0% win rate and 3 losses, even filtering out 1-2 loss signals improves win rate. May reduce signal count by 20-40% depending on how many Nifty 500 names have ADR below 1.8%. Small sample warning: 4 signals is insufficient to be highly confident — flag as MEDIUM.

proposals.title: Add intraday volume confirmation gate: require today's relative volume >= DZ_RETEST_REL_VOL_MIN at the time of the retest
proposals.proposed_change: Add a new constant DZ_RETEST_REL_VOL_MIN = 0.8. Load today's intraday 15m data (batch_15m is already available in _screen_demand_supply_zone — it is NOT currently loaded; add: batch_15m = _get_15m_batch()). Filter today's bars. Compute paced_vol and rel_vol_ratio exactly as in PDH and OI panels (paced_vol = (day_vol_so_far / elapsed_min) * 375, rel_vol_ratio = paced_vol / prev_vol where prev_vol = daily['Volume'].iloc[-2]). If rel_vol_ratio < DZ_RETEST_REL_VOL_MIN, skip (_dbg_fail 'retest_volume_too_low'). Insert after the proximity check (zone_dist_pct gate) and before the trade-plan computation. The threshold of 0.8 is deliberately lenient (below-average volume is OK for a zone retest, which is expected to be quiet before the bounce).
proposals.reasoning: Demand Zone has 2 signals with 0 wins and 2 expirations; Supply Zone has 1 signal with 0 wins and 1 expiration. All 3 signals expired — price reached the zone but never followed through. The current screener fires solely on proximity to a daily-chart zone with no intraday participation check: a stock can be near its zone on near-zero volume (thin tape, no real buyers/sellers showing up) and still generate a signal. Adding even a below-average volume filter (0.8x) ensures some intraday participation exists at the time of the retest. Small sample warning: 3 signals total is not statistically meaningful — this is a structural addition rather than a data-driven tune, but it closes an obvious logical gap.
proposals.expected_impact: Will reduce Demand/Supply Zone signals generated (filtering zero-participation retests). Will not fix the fundamental small-sample problem but prevents the panel from firing on completely illiquid retests. Likely reduces signal count by 15-30%.
